newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end steady in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end steady in thin trade.

text.p: Rubber futures were steady to slightly lower at the close on Thursday in thin trade with firm Japanese prices helping to shore up the local market, dealers said.
"Trading was thin and the only thing which held up the price here was the speculative buying which initially shored up prices in Japan," a local rubber trader said.
Prices of Tokyo's benchmark March contract dipped 0.2 yen to 137.2 while Kobe's March contract rose 0.2 yen from its settlement yesterday to 136.9.
Prices drifted in the absence of market-moving news, traders said.
"Prices were mostly steady, but the trading was really thin. One brand of rubber only traded about 100 tonnes. For the most part, it was a quiet market," another dealer said.
At around 0945 GMT, November RSS3 was seen at 124.25 U.S. cents a kg from 124.50 cents.

November RSS1 was seen at 176.50 Singapore cents (US$1.25) a kg from 176.25 cents. December TSR20 was seen at 171.00-173.00 Singapore cents (US$1.21-$1.22) a kg against the previous 173.50 cents. (US$1-S$1.41) -- Rene Pastor (65-870-3305)
